items.title: Govctl – A CLI enforcing RFC-driven discipline on AI coding
items.raw_excerpt: AI coding assistants are fast but undisciplined. They jump from idea to implementation without specification. Docs drift from code. "Best practices" become optional suggestions. I built govctl to fix this. It's an opinionated governance CLI that enforces phase discipline on software development: spec → impl → test → stable Every feature requires an RFC before implementation. Phases can't be skipped. Gates are checked, not suggested. items.title: AI 医疗还在比进度，百川已在比高度
items.raw_excerpt: 近一年来，AI 医疗正在进入一个明显不同于以往的新阶段。无论在国内还是海外，越来越多大型科技公司、医药企业和产业资本开始通过投资、并购或深度合作的方式，进入 AI 健康与医疗领域。 这背后并不只是对赛道规模的押注，而是一个更清晰的共识正在形成：医疗，正在成为少数真正需要、也能够检验大模型能力上限的核心场景之一。 但现实问题同样突出。尽管应用数量快速增长，受限于能力，真正能进入医疗核心流程的 AI依然有限。当前主流医疗大模型，大多仍建立在静态问答或医生角色扮演的范式之上，模型被要求给出看起来合理、语气专业的回答，却并不真正理解医疗决策是如何发生的。 在真实场景中，这类模型往往难以主动发现信息缺口，无法构建完整的医学推理路径，也缺乏对医疗幻觉的有效约束，最终只能反复输出模糊而安全的高频建议。这正是 AI 医疗看起来很热，但落地很难的根本原因。 行业真正需要的，并不是更像医生的回答，而是更接近医疗决策过程本身的模型能力。 百川给出的解法，正是从这一点切入。百川新一代医疗增强大语言模型 Baichuan-M3，没有继续强化问答或对话表现，而是将训练目标直接对准医疗决策过程本身。新的模型不再只负责生成结论，而是被训练为能够主动收集关键信息、构建医学推理路径，并在推理过程中持续抑制幻觉。这意味着，模型第一次被系统性地当作决策参与者，而不是回答生成器。 这种能力定义的变化，直接提升了模型在真实医疗场景中的可用性与可靠性。在多项医疗评测中，Baichuan-M3 已经展现出超越当前国际主流模型的表现，它的优势并不体现在表达更自然，而在于判断更稳定、推理更完整、风险更可控。 从更宏观的角度看，百川的路径，或许代表着 AI 医疗正在发生的一次重要转向：行业关注点正从模型能不能回答医学问题，转向模型是否能被信任地嵌入医疗系统。 当这一条件逐步成立，AI 医疗的价值，才可能真正从单点工具，演进为医

excerpt_i18n.zh: 近一年来，AI 医疗正在进入一个明显不同于以往的新阶段。无论在国内还是海外，越来越多大型科技公司、医药企业和产业资本开始通过投资、并购或深度合作的方式，进入 AI 健康与医疗领域。 这背后并不只是对赛道规模的押注，而是一个更清晰的共识正在形成：医疗，正在成为少数真正需要、也能够检验大模型能力上限的核心场景之一。 但现实问题同样突出。尽管应用数量快速增长，受限于能力，真正能进入医疗核心流程的 AI依然有限。当前主流医疗大模型，大多仍建立在静态问答或医生角色扮演的范式之上，模型被要求给出看起来合理、语气专业的回答，却并不真正理解医疗决策是如何发生的。 在真实场景中，这类模型往往难以主动发现信息缺口，无法构建完整的医学推理路径，也缺乏对医疗幻觉的有效约束，最终只能反复输出模糊而安全的高频建议。这正是 AI 医疗看起来很热，但落地很难的根本原因。 行业真正需要的，并不是更像医生的回答，而是更接近医疗决策过程本身的模型能力。 百川给出的解法，正是从这一点切入。百川新一代医疗增强大语言模型 Baichuan-M3，没有继续强化问答或对话表现，而是将训练目标直接对准医疗决策过程本身。新的模型不再只负责生成结论，而是被训练为能够主动收集关键信息、构建医学推理路径，并在推理过程中持续抑制幻觉。这意味着，模型第一次被系统性地当作决策参与者，而不是回答生成器。 这种能力定义的变化，直接提升了模型在真实医疗场景中的可用性与可靠性。在多项医疗评测中，Baichuan-M3 已经展现出超越当前国际主流模型的表现，它的优势并不体现在表达更自然，而在于判断更稳定、推理更完整、风险更可控。 从更宏观的角度看，百川的路径，或许代表着 AI 医疗正在发生的一次重要转向：行业关注点正从模型能不能回答医学问题，转向模型是否能被信任地嵌入医疗系统。 当这一条件逐步成立，AI 医疗的价值，才可能真正从单点工具，演进为医

Over the past year, AI in healthcare has entered a distinctly new phase. Both domestically and internationally, an increasing number of large tech companies, pharmaceutical firms, and industrial capital are entering the AI health and medical field through investments, mergers, acquisitions, or deep collaborations. This trend is not merely a bet on the scale of the sector but reflects a clearer consensus: healthcare is becoming one of the few core scenarios that genuinely require and can test the upper limits of large model capabilities.

However, practical challenges remain prominent. Despite the rapid growth in applications, AI that can truly integrate into core medical processes remains limited due to capability constraints. Most current mainstream medical large models are still built on paradigms of static Q&A or doctor role-playing, where models are expected to provide seemingly reasonable and professionally-toned responses without truly understanding how medical decisions are made.

In real-world scenarios, such models often struggle to proactively identify information gaps, construct complete medical reasoning pathways, or effectively constrain medical hallucinations, ultimately resorting to repeatedly outputting vague yet safe high-frequency advice. This is the fundamental reason why AI in healthcare appears promising but faces significant implementation challenges.

What the industry truly needs is not responses that mimic doctors more closely, but model capabilities that better approximate the medical decision-making process itself. Baichuan's solution addresses this exact point. Its new-generation enhanced medical large language model, Baichuan-M3, does not focus on strengthening Q&A or dialogue performance but instead targets the medical decision-making process directly in its training objectives. Ordering 40 cups of Bawang Tea's 'Bo Ya Jue Xian' in one go. Accessing over 50 government services on Alipay, including visas, household registration, and provident funds. Becoming an AI teaching assistant for every educator. On January 15, at the Qwen product launch event, Qwen officially announced its full integration into Alibaba's ecosystem, including Taobao, Alipay, Taobao Flash Sales, Fliggy, and Amap, rolling out over 400 new features at once, such as ordering takeout, shopping, and booking flights. AI is transitioning from chatting to getting things done. 

If this Qwen update is merely seen as "adding a few more Alibaba apps," its significance might be underestimated. Wu Jia, President of Alibaba Qwen's C-end Business Group, stated in the opening remarks, "Qwen is the first AI that can truly help you accomplish tasks." The new features span daily life, work, and education, each explained by three product managers on stage. While they may seem scattered, they point to the same shift—Qwen is evolving from a "chat assistant" to a "task assistant." As Wu Jia put it, AI is moving from the passenger seat to the driver's seat.

More importantly, in scenarios like food delivery and e-commerce, Qwen is touching "transactions" for the first time. Within Alibaba's ecosystem, once a product involves transactions, it is no longer an experimental offering but enters a genuine business validation phase. This Qwen update may set a new paradigm for the commercial application of AI models.

Only after achieving scale did Alibaba begin "discussing entry points." Looking back over the past year, the dominant form of C-end AI applications has largely remained confined to "solving problems within a dialog box."
